definitions.explanation: A pyramid in the geometric sense — a solid with a polygonal base and triangular faces meeting at a single point. Used for the abstract shape; the Egyptian monument is called ピラミッド.

examples.japanese: {四角錐|しかくすい}を{描|か}く。
{角錐|かくすい}の{体積|たいせき}を{求|もと}める。
examples.english: Find the volume of a pyramid.

examples.japanese: {底面|ていめん}が{三角形|さんかっけい}の{角錐|かくすい}を{三角錐|さんかくすい}と{呼|よ}ぶ。
examples.english: A pyramid whose base is a triangle is called a triangular pyramid (tetrahedron).

notes:
Compound of {角|かく} (corner; angle) + {錐|すい} (a tapering/awl-like shape). Used almost only in math class and technical contexts.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {三角錐|さんかくすい}: triangular pyramid (tetrahedron)
- {四角錐|しかくすい}: square pyramid
- {六角錐|ろっかくすい}: hexagonal pyramid

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {円錐|えんすい}: cone — circular base instead of polygonal
- {角柱|かくちゅう}: prism — two parallel polygonal faces instead of a point at the top
- ピラミッド: pyramid (Egyptian monument; loanword)
